deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck's derivator-style homotopy theory (1982 onward). The notes work with a derivator D, cohomology H_D(X, ξ) of a small category X with coefficients ξ ∈ D(X), and the class W_D of 'D-equivalences': functors u for which u^* induces isomorphisms on H_D for all coefficients. X is covered by two 'open' subcategories U and U' (sieves or cosieves) with intersection U∩U'.

Previous page. X̄ → X is a weak equivalence with a functor φ: X̄ → Ψ, where Ψ = Q − {e}, Q = Δ¹×Δ¹ and e = (1,1). Set γ_0 = φ_*(ξ) and γ = k_*(γ_0), where k: Ψ ↪ Q. Since e is a final object of Q, γ(e) = H_D(Q, γ) ≅ H_D(X, ξ). Hence the Mayer–Vietoris square (**) is the value of a right Kan extension along Ψ ↪ Q. That square is
- H_D(X) → H_D(U) and H_D(X) → H_D(U'),
- H_D(U) → H_D(U∩U') ← H_D(U').
So (**) is homotopy cartesian in D(e). Pullbacks of isomorphisms are isomorphisms, so i_0^* iso ⇒ i^* iso, where i_0 and i are parallel edges. Since this holds for all ξ, i_0 ∈ W_D ⇒ i ∈ W_D.

This page. Grothendieck asks for the converse, i ∈ W_D ⇒ i_0 ∈ W_D. He observes it would follow if (**), or the coherent square that produces it, were also cocartesian, i.e. bicartesian. His 'morale':
- Cartesianness of (**) is the cohomological translation of the fact that the square of categories U∩U' → U, U' → X is cocartesian in a sufficiently strong sense (homotopy pushout/excision).
- That square of categories is also trivially cartesian, since U∩U' = U ×_X U'.
- So one may expect, 'under certain conditions', that its image under H_D(−, ξ) is cocartesian.

He then fixes notation: Q = Δ¹×Δ¹ and Ψ = Q − {e}. He notes that Ψ_Q(X) restricted to Ψ is Ψ_Ψ(X), already studied. On the next page Ψ_Q(X) is identified with the square of inclusions, and he formulates a 'Principe (P)': the Grothendieck construction of a span in Cat maps to X by a weak equivalence. In modern terms this is the homotopy-pushout/excision statement, in the spirit of Thomason's hocolim theorem.
errors: No outright error: the sufficient condition (bicartesian square ⇒ iso on one edge iff iso on the parallel edge) is correct.

The hedge 'sous certaines conditions' is essential. For a non-stable D (e.g. the derivator of homotopy types, where W_D is ordinary weak equivalences), cohomology turns cocartesian squares into cartesian ones, but not cartesian squares into cocartesian ones. The converse i ∈ W_D ⇒ i_0 ∈ W_D then fails. Example: A acyclic but not contractible, U = CA, U' = pt, U∩U' = A, X = ΣA ≃ pt. Here U → X is an equivalence but A → pt is not.
For stable (triangulated) derivators, cartesian ⇔ cocartesian, so the converse holds automatically. Grothendieck does not make this explicit here.
The machine transcription garbles the formula: it should read i ∈ W_D ⇒ i_0 ∈ W_D, not i^t.

ideas.what: Mayer–Vietoris square for a two-set cover of a category obtained as a right Kan extension along Ψ ↪ Δ¹×Δ¹, hence homotopy cartesian; consequence i_0 ∈ W_D ⇒ i ∈ W_D
ideas.modern_name: Mayer–Vietoris / homotopy pullback squares in a derivator; excision for D-equivalences
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Les Dérivateurs); developed by Maltsiniotis, Cisinski, Groth
ideas.where_published: Related material in Les Dérivateurs (circulated manuscript, ed. Künzer–Malgoire–Maltsiniotis); Maltsiniotis, Astérisque 301

ideas.what: Converse requires the cohomological square to be bicartesian, i.e. 'cartesian ⇒ cocartesian' for the image of a cartesian (and cocartesian) square of categories
ideas.modern_name: Bicartesian squares; stability of derivators (cartesian ⇔ cocartesian)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Maltsiniotis; Groth ('Derivators, pointed derivators and stable derivators', 2013); Franke; Heller
ideas.where_published: Les Dérivateurs discusses triangulated derivators; exact statement unsure

ideas.what: Heuristic: homological cartesianness ↔ strong cocartesianness (homotopy pushout) of the cover square of categories
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy pushout of open covers / Thomason's homotopy colimit theorem / excision in a fundamental localizer
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (asphericity and localizer theory), unsure for this exact form

missed.claim: Grothendieck raises, without resolving, the question of which derivators D (or which conditions) make i ∈ W_D ⇒ i_0 ∈ W_D hold for all two-set covers by sieves, i.e. a 'two-sided excision' property of the localizer W_D. This is true for stable/homological D and false for homotopy types (acyclic-space counterexample). A clean characterization of the localizers satisfying it is a natural question; it is likely implicit in later work on stable derivators and homological localizers rather than new.
missed.quote: on peut s'attendre (sous certaines conditions...) que le diagramme transformé par H^i_D(-,ξ) soit cocartésien
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would link the stability of D to an excision property of the class W_D of D-equivalences. Modest interest; probably close to known results.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine working-out of Mayer–Vietoris and bicartesian squares in the derivator setting. The heuristic is sound and the hedge appropriate, but nothing here goes beyond what stable-derivator theory and Thomason/Cisinski later made standard.
